events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $7.11 (model confidence 0.83)
events.body:
The trip is RydeTAXI and metered, so detour kilometres feed the fare: the excess-distance line is $7.50 for 5.32 km x $1.4102/km [F4][F7]. The trace confirms one off-route segment (23:03-23:14, 7.28 km where the optimal route covers 2.25 km, adding 5.04 km) [F3], so RD-1 engages and each segment must be tested against RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5.

RD-4 (a) fails as settled by the trace: no LTA traffic incident is recorded near the route [F15], and RD-4 (b) cannot exempt on its own - the KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY speed band 2 (10-19 km/h) record is corroboration only, and in any event it covers 22:40-23:03 while other corridors recorded band 5 [F12][F13][F14][RD-4].

On RD-5, the rider's only message before the segment is "Sure, no problem" at 23:00, replying to the driver's 22:59 proposal to "go round via Upper Paya Lebar Road" - before the 23:03 segment start [F8][F9][F10]. That is a specific named-road agreement, not a general "whichever way is faster" authority, so it covers driving on Upper Paya Lebar Road only [RD-5]. The driver's own post-trip statement places the driven path elsewhere: "In the end I went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead because it looked clearer" [F11]. The agreement to Upper Paya Lebar Road therefore does not cover the road actually driven - the very point that makes the complaint coherent. His assertion of the rider's agreement is neither consent to a different road nor, appearing only in his statement, consent at all [F11][RD-5]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped, so no missing record forces the consent question to a human [F10].

Refund: the unexcused segment's extra km, 5.04 km, at this trip's own per-km rate ($26.30 / 18.65 km = $1.4102/km) = $7.107, rounded to $7.11 [F3][F7][RD-2]. The rate is taken as the fare record states it, unrounded [F4]. The residual 0.28 km of excess distance (5.32 km billed less 5.04 km in the measured segment) is corridor/match noise outside any segment and is not refunded [F4][F7][RD-2]. Waiting time of $0.11 (0.4 min) is properly charged on RydeTAXI under the meter and is not refunded [F5][RD-3]. No unpublished surcharge appears - platform fee $1.47, no surge - so FARE-1 adds nothing [F6][F7][FARE-1]. The driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes, so the repeated-breach flag of RD-6 is not triggered, and profile facts could not decide the case alone in any event [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement in context [F8][F9][F11]. They contain a route argument only - no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence: the trace settles the incident screen and the segment measurement, the chat is complete and timestamped, and the driver has himself stated which route he took, so every element the ruling needs is settled [F3][F10][F11][F15]. Because the off-route segment counts, the outcome is refund_partial, not no_action as both briefs requested.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We looked into your trip and found you were driven on a road other than the one you and your driver agreed on. You agreed to go via Upper Paya Lebar Road, but the driver went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead, and that stretch added about 5 km to your fare. As a result, we're refunding $7.11 to you as a Ryde voucher. Nothing changes on your account — no action is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed the trip and found that a road other than the one you agreed with the rider was driven. You and the rider settled on Upper Paya Lebar Road, but your own account says you went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead, and that stretch was longer than the most direct route. $7.11 of the fare will be refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. Please treat an agreed road as the route to drive. No further action on your account this time.

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 23:03:00 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount.
